labs.title: Govern Copilot interactions with retention and DLP
labs.summary: Use Microsoft Purview to create a Copilot retention policy and a Copilot-scoped DLP policy, review simulation results, and turn on enforcement.
labs.scenario: Contoso is expanding Microsoft 365 Copilot and wants guardrails in place first. In the **simulated Microsoft Purview** portal, create a retention policy with the current **Microsoft Copilot experiences** location. Then create a DLP policy for **Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat** that prevents Copilot from processing items labeled **Highly Confidential**, test it in simulation mode, and turn it on after review.
learningObjectives: Identify the current Purview retention location for Copilot and AI app interactions
Create a DLP policy scoped to Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat
Use sensitivity labels to exclude protected content from Copilot processing
Deploy DLP through simulation before enforcement
prerequisites: Know the purpose of retention, DLP, and sensitivity labels in Microsoft Purview

checklist.name: Create Copilot DLP policy in simulation

steps.title: Create a Copilot retention policy
steps.instruction: Open **Data lifecycle management > Retention policies**, select **New retention policy**, and create **Copilot interactions retention**. For **Locations**, select **Microsoft Copilot experiences** only, choose **Retain items for the organization period and then delete**, and turn the policy on.
steps.hint: Do not use the older combined Teams chats and Copilot interactions wording for this new policy.
steps.explanation: Retention for Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat is now separate from Teams chats. The Microsoft Copilot experiences location covers supported Copilot interactions for compliance retention.

rules.description: Retention policy targets Microsoft Copilot experiences
rules.failureFeedback: Create the retention policy with Microsoft Copilot experiences as the location.

steps.title: Start a custom DLP policy
steps.instruction: Open **Data Loss Prevention > Policies**, select **Create policy**, and choose **Custom policy**.
steps.hint: The Copilot policy location is available from the Custom policy template.
steps.explanation: Copilot-specific DLP uses its own location rather than combining Exchange or SharePoint in the same policy.

steps.title: Scope DLP to Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat
steps.instruction: Name the policy **Block Highly Confidential content in Copilot**. On **Locations**, select only **Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat**.
steps.hint: Do not add Exchange email or SharePoint sites in this Copilot-specific policy.
steps.explanation: The Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat location applies controls when Copilot processes prompts, files, and emails in supported experiences.

rules.description: DLP policy uses only the Copilot location

match.name: Block Highly Confidential content in Copilot

rules.failureFeedback: Use only the Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat location.

steps.title: Block processing of Highly Confidential content
steps.instruction: In **Rules**, use **Content contains > Sensitivity labels**, select **Highly Confidential**, and choose **Prevent Copilot from processing content**.
steps.hint: This applies to labeled files and emails Copilot might otherwise use as grounding data.
steps.explanation: Sensitivity-label-based DLP can exclude labeled files and emails from Copilot processing while the user’s original access remains governed by Microsoft 365 permissions.

steps.title: Run the DLP policy in simulation mode
steps.instruction: Set **Policy state** to **Run the policy in simulation mode** and create the policy. Open it and select **Review simulation results**.
steps.hint: Simulation audits impact without enforcing actions.
steps.explanation: Simulation mode lets admins validate policy scope and tune exceptions before the policy affects users.

rules.description: Simulation mode was used and reviewed

match.name: Block Highly Confidential content in Copilot

rules.failureFeedback: Create in simulation mode and review results.

steps.title: Turn on the DLP policy after review
steps.instruction: In **Policy state**, change the policy to **Turn it on** and select **Save**.
steps.hint: The form will not save enforcement until simulation results have been reviewed.
steps.explanation: A staged deployment balances protection with change management: observe first, then enforce once the policy behaves as intended.

steps.title: Verify retention and DLP governance
steps.instruction: Return to **Retention policies** and **Data Loss Prevention > Policies** to verify the retention policy is on and DLP is enforcing the Highly Confidential label rule.
steps.hint: Both policies should be complete in the checklist.
steps.explanation: Retention preserves interaction records for compliance, while DLP reduces the sensitive content Copilot can process.

labs.solution:
1. Open **Data lifecycle management > Retention policies** and select **New retention policy**.
2. Create **Copilot interactions retention**. Select **Microsoft Copilot experiences** only, choose **Retain items for the organization period and then delete**, and turn it on.
3. Open **Data Loss Prevention > Policies** and select **Create policy** > **Custom policy**.
4. Name it **Block Highly Confidential content in Copilot**. Select only **Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat**.
5. In **Rules**, choose **Content contains > Sensitivity labels**, select **Highly Confidential**, and set **Prevent Copilot from processing content**.
6. Set **Policy state** to **Run the policy in simulation mode**, create it, open it, and select **Review simulation results**.
7. Change **Policy state** to **Turn it on** and save. Simulation mode, DLP alerts, and notifications are supported for this location; wording stays conservative because rollout details can vary by tenant.
